checks: Checked the four-fiber source §§1–3 and the extension in §6. Adjacent fixed intervals force an interior replacement to contain the unit interval. Among the two sides, one contains two consecutive fixed sites since 2m≥4. The closer site is the midpoint of the replacement and the farther site, which also forces the replacement inside the unit interval. At an endpoint only the upper containment is required.

Each one-site shrink is realized by its exposed-base hull inside the old rectangle. A singleton gives zero endpoint measure. Additional null sites outside the positive base hull have depth zero by pure-base separation; no intermediate null site inside this hull is possible under convexity.

The four displayed caps cover the integer chain in left and right pairs. Each cap includes m−1 whole unit fibers and one half fiber at its central base in the original body. A single shrink keeps this bound and leaves a symmetric odd block of mass 2m−1 around an actual integer mark, attaining the raw upper bound by reflection.

For paired centered shrink the roof slope changes give actual fibers, including t=0. The same caps have mass m−3/2+t. The indicated symmetric block contains 2m−3 full fibers and two intervals of length t, giving the matching lower bound. Division by the true totals yields the two displayed ratios with opposite strict monotonicity.

overlap.comparison: Gives a general piecewise-affine raw-depth algorithm on positive compatible intervals. It does not give the universal single-site obstruction, coordinated path, or limiting depth at endpoint deletion.

readability: The paired ratio is 1/2 minus the reciprocal of twice the current mass, so its derivative has the asserted sign even at m=2. The t=0 normalized value includes no mass from the endpoint singletons.
review_method: Independent cold proof read, source-locator comparison, predecessor proof comparison, and exact arithmetic replay where relevant.
summary: The even interval chain has the stated exact raw maxima and opposite normalized monotonicity for one and two endpoint trims.
